answer: In an agent market trading opal and copper, votes on disputed trades are weighted by escrowed stake, not account count. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand identities still buys only 100 tokens of voting power, so a tide of new accounts adds no influence by itself. To control a vote, an attacker must acquire enough stake to outweigh honest voters and lock it through the dispute period, tying up capital and bearing its price risk.
